sections.h2: Where is Ridgefield, CT, and what is the town like?
sections.html:
Ridgefield is a town in Fairfield County on the New York state border, with a 2020 census population of 25,033. It covers about 35 square miles and borders Danbury to the north, Wilton to the south and Redding to the east, with Lewisboro, North Salem and Southeast in New York to the west.

The terrain is hilly and rocky. Elevation runs from about 342 feet at Branchville to 1,060 feet at Pine Mountain, and glaciers left rocks scattered across the landscape. Public open space totals roughly 5,200 acres, about 23 percent of the town.

Those hills affect a house. Driveway grade and drainage are details Ridgefield buyers and inspectors will ask about.

Ridgefield was settled in 1708 by English colonists from Norwalk who bought the land from Chief Catoonah, and it was incorporated in 1709. For most of its history it was farm country.

The Battle of Ridgefield took place on April 27, 1777, when colonial forces under General David Wooster and Benedict Arnold met a British force returning from a raid on Danbury. The Keeler Tavern, still standing at 132 Main Street, has a British cannonball lodged in its side.

In the late nineteenth century the railroad connection and cooler hill elevation drew wealthy New Yorkers, who built large estates. After the Great Depression many of those estates were broken up, and subdivisions of one- and two-acre lots turned the town into a commuter suburb in the 1950s through the 1970s. The population rose from 4,356 in 1950 to 18,188 in 1970.

The Lounsbury House at 316 Main Street, built around 1896 by Governor Phineas Chapman Lounsbury, is now the Ridgefield Veterans Memorial Community Center. Other National Register listings include the Benedict House and Shop on Rockwell Road, the Lewis June House on North Salem Road and the Thomas Hyatt House on Barlow Mountain Road.

The result is a mix of historic village houses, farmhouses, large estate remnants and mid-century subdivision homes.

The government line is worth knowing. Ridgefield elects its Planning and Zoning Commission, Board of Appeals on Zoning and Board of Tax Review, so most land-use and assessment questions go to those local boards rather than a city department.

sections.h2: Which villages and neighborhoods make up Ridgefield?
sections.html:
Ridgefield has several village areas and about nineteen named neighborhoods. The villages include Ridgefield (the town center), Branchville, Ridgebury, Titicus and Farmingville.

  • Ridgefield center: the Main Street area, with the Ridgefield Center Historic District listed on the National Register in 1984.
  • Branchville: in the southeast corner, home to the Metro-North station.
  • Ridgebury: the northern section, where Boehringer Ingelheim's U.S. headquarters sits.
  • Farmingville, Titicus, Limestone, Flat Rock and Florida: other locales named around the town center.
  • West Mountain, Cooper Hill, Topstone, Twixt Hills and Long Ridge: among the named residential neighborhoods.

If your house is in or near the historic district, ask the town about any rules before planning exterior changes or a sale prep project.

sections.h2: What is the geology under a Ridgefield house?
sections.html:
Ridgefield sits on bedrock that varies across town. Cameron's Line, a fault formed some 250 million years ago, runs across the southern half, and light earthquakes are occasionally felt along it. North of the line the ground is rich in limestone, which was mined and burned in kilns in the nineteenth century.

Why it matters for a sale: buyers and inspectors ask about ledge, drainage and well water on hilly lots, and a seller who knows the answers closes faster.

sections.h2: What does the weather mean for a Ridgefield home?
sections.html:
Ridgefield averages about 53 inches of rainfall a year, and the climate table on Wikipedia shows an average January high of 36 degrees and low of 19. Record highs and lows run from 106 to minus 18.

Check your gutters, grading and sump pump, and note any past water in the basement, because buyers ask. Winter cold stresses pipes and roofs, so keep heat on in a vacant property and document recent roof or furnace work.

sections.h2: Who works in Ridgefield, and how do people commute?
sections.html:
The largest industry in town is Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, whose United States headquarters is in the Ridgebury section.

Commuters have options. The Metro-North Danbury Branch serves Branchville station, with trains going north to Danbury and south to South Norwalk. At peak hours some trains continue to Stamford and some express trains reach Grand Central Terminal. Housatonic Area Regional Transit runs a weekday commuter shuttle between Katonah station and park-and-ride lots at 207 Main Street and 58 Prospect Ridge.

Ridgefield also has cultural draws that buyers mention, including the Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum, the Ridgefield Playhouse, the Keeler Tavern Museum and the Weir Farm National Historic Site on the Wilton border. Weir Farm is one of only two National Park Service units in the state.

Homes within reach of the Branchville station are easier to describe to commuters, so mention the distance to the platform in any listing or offer discussion.

sections.h2: What are the public schools in Ridgefield?
sections.html:
Ridgefield Public Schools runs nine schools: six elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school. The elementary schools are Veterans Park, Branchville, Farmingville, Scotland, Barlow Mountain and Ridgebury. The middle schools are Scotts Ridge and East Ridge, and the high school is Ridgefield High School, home of the Tigers.

The town also has private options, including St. Mary School, St. Padre Pio Academy and Ridgefield Academy. Buyers with children will check which elementary school serves an address, so have that answer ready.

sections.h2: How are water and utilities handled in Ridgefield?
sections.html:
Aquarion Water Company serves the central and western parts of Ridgefield, while small water companies serve some other areas. Eversource provides electricity. Telephone and internet service comes from Frontier Communications and Comcast.

The water line was extended up North Street to Barlow Mountain and Scotland Elementary Schools in recent years. Because service coverage differs by street, ask the town or the water provider which utility serves your address before you answer a buyer's question about a well or public water.

sections.h2: How is a Ridgefield sale recorded and what does the state require?
sections.html:
The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Connecticut Form OP-236 with the town clerk when the deed is recorded in Ridgefield. The state says the tax is due when the consideration is two thousand dollars or more, unless an exemption applies.

  • If the seller is an estate, trust, LLC, partnership or S corporation, or there are more than two sellers, Schedule A is attached.
  • If there is more than one buyer, Schedule B is attached.
  • A transfer between spouses is one of the listed exemptions.

Rates depend on price and change over time, so confirm the exact amount with your closing attorney or the Ridgefield town clerk. Questions about local assessment, appeals or a tax balance go to the Ridgefield assessor and tax collector.

faqs.a: Ridgefield covers about 35 square miles in Fairfield County and had 25,033 residents in the 2020 census. It borders Danbury, Wilton, Redding and three New York towns.

faqs.q: Is there train service in Ridgefield?
faqs.a: Yes, Metro-North's Danbury Branch serves Branchville station in the southeast corner of town. Some peak trains continue to Stamford and some express trains reach Grand Central Terminal.
Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals is the town's largest industry, with its U.S. headquarters in the Ridgebury section.
Aquarion serves the central and western parts of town, and small water companies serve some other areas. Check your address with the provider.

faqs.q: What form do I file when I sell a house in Ridgefield?
faqs.a: The seller files Connecticut Form OP-236, the conveyance tax return, with the town clerk when the deed is recorded. Your closing attorney normally prepares it.
